SPECIAL-105x210_biohackers-zine-timeline.title: BIOHACKERS TIMELINE: AN ARCHAEOLOGY OF THE WETWARE FRONTIER
SPECIAL-105x210_biohackers-zine-timeline.analysis: A cyber-tropical chronopolitics unfolds: the timeline rewires dominant narratives of innovation, tracing a cartography where biohacking germinates not only in Californian garages but in Indonesian warungs, Swiss squats, and Indian makerspaces. The zine becomes a sedimented memory, an archaeo-futurist device that excavates forgotten kitchens and repurposed rice cookers as ancestral bioreactors.

fragments.text: 2008 — The first DIYbio group, DIYbio Boston, starts shaking Erlenmeyers in a shared kitchen. Garage labs mutate from computer overclocking into genetic insurgency.
2011 — Hackteria Network emerges from a Yogyakarta kitchen, fusing Javanese fermentation with open-source microscopy. The Global South writes its own biohacking sutra.

biohaha-helmi_hardian-angela_sunaryo-zin.title: SENSEWALKING FLUX: ELECTROMAGNETIC DRIFT IN THE URBAN HUMUS
biohaha-helmi_hardian-angela_sunaryo-zin.analysis: This zine is a hacker-ethnography of the sensory undercommons, where DIY electronics become prosthetic ears for hearing the city's electromagnetic gut flora. Sensewalking unfolds as a decolonial practice, attuning the walker to spectral ecologies that colonial cartography never registered — a flux between Javanese mysticism, circuit bending, and the humus of informal markets.

fragments.text: We built a dirt-cheap EMF sniffer from a scrap radio, an LED, and a tamarind candy wrapper. The city screams in 50 Hz, and the durian seller’s fridge sings a low G.
Walking barefoot through Pasar Burung, the bioelectric field of caged songbirds registers as a shimmering texture — a feathered internet predating fiber optics.

IGEM-Comic-2010_artscienceBLR.pdf.title: iGEM 2010: SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY AS SPECULATIVE KANNADA COMEDY
IGEM-Comic-2010_artscienceBLR.pdf.analysis: artscienceBLR fuses synthetic biology with the graphic sensibility of Indian street pamphlets, producing a comic that treats genetic circuits as bazaar-bargain gods. The zine’s visual vernacular indigenizes the iGEM imaginary, embedding engineered bacteria within the everyday fabulations of Bangalore’s cyber-tropical chai stalls and auto-rickshaws, challenging the sterile lab aesthetic with microbial carnival.

fragments.text: Panel shows a bacterium in a petri dish wearing a Mysore turban, splicing genes with a tiny machete. Caption: ‘When life gives you plasmids, make parkour.’
The lab transforms into a kitchen; the protagonist's grandmother brews kombucha with a synthetic noise-generating SCOBY that sings like a veena in quorum-sensing quavers.

BubblePunk Zine Printy PDF.pdf.title: BUBBLEPUNK: SOAP FILM AS DIGITAL NATURALISM INTERFACE
BubblePunk Zine Printy PDF.pdf.analysis: BubblePunk reimagines digital naturalism through the medium of soap, treating bubbles as minimal computation surfaces that sense humidity, wind, and insect flight. The zine is a hacker-ethnography of froth — a punk craft that displaces silicon with surfactant skins, constructing a tropical physics of transient interfaces where the computational is breathed, not built.

fragments.text: A dragonfly's wing beat soaks into a soap membrane, translating turbulence into algorithmic color. The bubble becomes a screenless display, a living pixel made of air and stolen detergent.
We built a bubble bot from a gutted printer and a terracotta pot. It exhales frothy geometries that trap the jungle’s humidity as ephemeral, iridescent data visualizations.

microzineinglescomLAST.pdf.title: SOIL SPECTRALITIES: DIY MICROSCOPY IN THE RIZOSPHERIC UNDERWORLD
microzineinglescomLAST.pdf.analysis: This zine performs a tropical soil inquiry, merging frugal microscopy with peasant epistemologies. It constitutes an underground archive where the rhizosphere’s micro-politics become legible through hacker optics, framing soil as a spectral commons — a medium where ancestral agricultural knowledge and DIY bio-observation fuse into a political ecology of decay and regeneration.

fragments.text: My microscope is a hacked webcam lens taped to a discarded plastic slide holder, illuminated by a stolen streetlamp’s LED. In this tiny theater I watch nematodes waltz through humus like ghosts of fermented monsoons.

The sample from the burnt rice field reveals a cosmos: fungal hyphae weaving phosphorus songs, bacteria in quorum, a tardigrade dreaming in sugar cane ash. Soil health is a conversation between the dead and the yet-to-be-planted.

CRISPR_19thCentury_1x_126x210.pdf.title: CRISPR IN THE AGE OF STEAM: ANACHRONISTIC GENE-SCISSOR FICTIONS
CRISPR_19thCentury_1x_126x210.pdf.analysis: A hacker-ethnography of speculative histories, this zine deploys AI to conjure a 19th-century Java where CRISPR is an autochthonous fantasy — gene editing imagined not through laboratory modernity but through gamelan rhythms, batik patterns, and plantation botany. It unearths a decolonial counter-memory, proposing that the genetic repair kit was already latent in the tropical imaginary, waiting for a steam-powered application.

fragments.text: An AI-generated lithograph depicts a Victorian batik-clad scientist injecting a dragonfly with a clockwork syringe filled with glowing ‘inheritance particles’ harvested from a Dutch-tea plantation’s clonal tea bushes — colonial science rewritten as Jawa-punk.
Caption: ‘Using Siamang Cas9, Madame Suryaningsih edited the hue of her orchid’s lip to match the exact color of the 1883 Krakatau sunset remembered in family lore.’

HackteriaTaxidermiaZine_A5_Screen.pdf.title: TAXIDERMIA DEL MERDEK: HACKER PRESERVATION OF MOIST ANIMALITIES
HackteriaTaxidermiaZine_A5_Screen.pdf.analysis: HackteriaTaxidermia rewires taxidermy as a postcolonial bio-art, rejecting the vitrine of conquest for an intimate, feminist ritual of animal re-companioning. The zine registers as a Cyber-Tropical witch’s manual: preservation becomes an act of honouring the moist remains of the rainforest, blending Javanese herbal knowledge with open-source chemistry, crafting cyborg-animal-spirit objects that murmur with ancestral humidity.

fragments.text: We collected a dead tokek from the forest floor near the temple, and preserved him with borax sourced from a local goldsmith. His skin now holds stories of gecko-djinns and polysaccharide sutures.
fragments.source: Story: The Tokek that Wouldn't Fade

fragments.text: DIY taxidermy is not trophy-making but a ritual of re-kinship: we fill the empty bodies with tamarind paste, myrrh, and a tiny voice recorder that loops whispered Karawitan when the room humidity rises above 80%.

BAJRA DIWO READ.pdf.title: BAJRA DIWO: CULTIVATING CODE IN THE TERRACED MUD
BAJRA DIWO READ.pdf.analysis: BAJRA DIWO documents an art-science collaboration that refuses the extractive model of citizen science, insisting instead that the terraced landscape is already a cosmological technology. The zine emerges as a hacker-ethnography of the Sawah, where code is composted with myth, and sensors become offering bowls — a Cyber-Tropical praxis where silicon learns to bow.

fragments.text: We planted RFID tags in Javanese rice paddies to listen to the water’s flow logic; the farmers already knew that the paddy sings a different tune before the harvest moon. Now we have spectrograms of that ancient song.

Art-science in Indonesia means you cannot separate the microcontroller from the myth of Dewi Sri. Every sensor must acknowledge the goddess of rice, or the data comes out bitter and the circuit refuses to boot.

HLab14_FullBook_inside.pdf.title: HACKTERIALAB 2014 — YOGYAKARTA: FERMENTATION, FOREST, AND THE FUGITIVE LABORATORY
HLab14_FullBook_inside.pdf.analysis: HLab14’s full documentation is a hacker-ethnography of a 10-day temporary autonomous zone in Yogyakarta, where Taiwanese bio-artists, Swiss circuit benders, and Javanese dukun smoked local tobacco while extracting DNA from river clams. The zine’s fragments perform a Cyber-Tropical sensorium: open-source hardware mingles with ritual, fermentation becomes a biological post-studio practice, and the laboratory dissolves into the jungle’s continuous rumour.

fragments.text: In the kampung, we built a microscope from coconut shell and a smartphone; the sample was a drop of jamu from the Ibu next door — a cosmos of lactobacilli that had been domesticated for generations, now captured in our open-source lens.

The forest workshop became a fugitive biolab: we fermented palm wine with wild yeasts collected from the tail feathers of a brahminy kite, documenting the process with a hacked Super 8 camera running on bicycle dynamo.

HLab14_FullBook_CoverFront.pdf.title: HLab14 COVER: THE ICONOGRAPHY OF A TROPICAL HACKER CONVERGENCE
HLab14_FullBook_CoverFront.pdf.analysis: This cover operates as a compressed manifesto: bamboo microscopy, phage puppets, and edible microcontrollers encode a Cyber-Tropical visual language where lab equipment is re-territorialized by the Javanese everyday. The publication context signals a distributed, feminist print ecology — risograph-duplicated by collectives who treat the zine as a spore, meant to circulate through village libraries, artisanal coffee shops, and international biohackerspaces alike.

fragments.text: The front cover is a risograph-printed assembly of a microscope lens made from a woven bamboo funnel, a durian cracked open to reveal an Arduino, and a shadow puppet of a phage. Text reads: 'HackteriaLab 2014 — Yogyakarta' in hand-carved font that mimics banana leaf etching.

Design by the TempehLab collective: a gestural taxonomy of tropical biohacking rendered in three colors — turmeric yellow, palm sap green, and the magenta of fermented beetroot. The ISBN is embedded inside a drawing of a rice grain.

HLab14_FullBook_CoverBack.pdf.title: HLab14 Book – Back Cover
HLab14_FullBook_CoverBack.pdf.analysis: The reverse mirror of the HLab14 compendium: a test pattern of bio-hacker ritual, where the remnants of wetware circuits, fermented inks, and collective field notes bleed through the cardboard spine. This cover-back doubles as a sigil for the lab that never ends—an onto-graphic surface that maps the backstage of open source biology.

fragments.text: The verso of a communal mycelium – spores of documentation cling to its surface, ready to germinate in other latitudes.

thGAP_booklet_print.pdf.title: thGAP Booklet (already catalogued)
thGAP_booklet_print.pdf.analysis: Previously detailed in the Arai-eek Deep Info Dossier. Refer to earlier entry for full poetic annotation, themes of trans hackfeminism, and the thGAP wetlab protocols.

fragments.text: Already woven into the dossier’s mangrove archive – skip or revisit the original node.

ZhTrans_OpenLetterToLuluAndNana.pdf.title: Open Letter to Lulu and Nana: An Ethical/Poetic Analysis
ZhTrans_OpenLetterToLuluAndNana.pdf.analysis: A sororal transmission to the first CRISPR-edited humans, written from the margins where transgenic and transgender identities collide. The zine unravels the colonial grammars of genetic enhancement, countering the techno-patriarchal narratives with a transfeminist poetics of care. Lulu and Nana are addressed not as objects of experiment but as kin in a damaged lineage, their genomes entangled with histories of racialized science and the queer promise of intentional mutation.

fragments.text: A letter that travels through the double helix like a monsoon – wet, unresolved, and full of the ancestral murmurs that gene-editing scissors cannot cut.

A3_trippleNarrow.pdf.title: Tripple Narrow: Design/Layout Experimental Zine
A3_trippleNarrow.pdf.analysis: A folding manifesto where the grid is a spine and the text becomes a choreographic score. Triple Narrow columns on A3 sheets whisper the secret geometry of risograph dreams, urging the reader to inhabit the space between columns as a political act. This zine is a paper DNA origami, teaching the body how to read otherwise.

fragments.text: A typographic triptych that breathes with the humidity of the printing press; folds are the hinges of a new visual vernacular.

Jornadas THF wetlab hangar 2021 zine baj.title: Jornadas TransHackFeminist Wetlab: Hangar Barcelona 2021
Jornadas THF wetlab hangar 2021 zine baj.analysis: Decanted from the wetlab encounter at Hangar, this zine captures the somatic protocols shared during the Jornadas THF: centrifuging urine for estrogen, building DIY speculums, cooking herbal contraceptives, and scripting collective care circuits. ‘Baja’ signals the low-resolution, lo-fi transmission of knowledge – deliberately degraded to avoid capture by sterile academia. The pages smell of agar, yerba mate, and solidarity.

fragments.text: A tropical depression that formed in the Mediterranean humidity of bodily fluids, leaving a fertile deposit of protocols on the shores of the zine.

Genital_Panic_Marry_Magic.pdf.title: Genital Panic, Marry Magic: Estrogenic Biopolitics
Genital_Panic_Marry_Magic.pdf.analysis: A grimoire where the anxious genital is alchemized into nuptial sorcery. Mary Maggic charts the colonial circulation of estrogen molecules through rivers, urine, and pharma-capital, proposing an unholy matrimony between the body’s leaky borders and the magic of DIY hormone extraction. The zine is a ritual manual for domesticating the molecular uncanny, where the panic of VALIE EXPORT meets the sticky euphoria of open source hormones.

fragments.text: A spell cast in the flooded basement of the Anthropocene – estrogen becomes a monsoon river, marrying bodies as it dissolves borders.

EZTROZINE_ISI_HVS100_2MK LONG_@2X.pdf.title: Open Source Estrogen Guide / Panduan Estrogen Sumber Terbuka
EZTROZINE_ISI_HVS100_2MK LONG_@2X.pdf.analysis: A step-by-step riverine pamphlet for liberating estrogen from urine, printed in the tropical long-format that mimics the flowing waterways of Jogjakarta. The guide walks the reader through collecting, hydrolyzing, and identifying estrogens using rudimentary kitchen chemistry and a hacked laser spectrometer. Bilingual incantations in Bahasa Indonesia and English make the protocol a commons, not a patent.

fragments.text: A mangrove of a manual – its roots tangled in local pharmacopeia, its canopy breathing the fog of global endocrine disruption.

EZTROZINE_COVER_IV230_2MK LONG_2X.pdf.title: Eztrozine Cover Art
EZTROZINE_COVER_IV230_2MK LONG_2X.pdf.analysis: The vibrant threshold to the estrogenic manual: a halftone collage of molecular mandalas, menstrual blood moon phases, and the specter of a homemade spectrometer. Designed to be detached and used as a ritual poster, the cover entices with the promise that the body’s hidden rivers can be mapped, and their chemicals made visible.

fragments.text: A retina-print of the endocrine sea; this cover is a portal, not a wrapper.

Transcriptions Zine, First Edition, Spri.title: Transcriptions Zine, First Edition, Spring 2022
Transcriptions Zine, First Edition, Spri.analysis: A spliced transcript of lived experiments, where western blot memoirs leak into estrogenic verse, and pipette tips are held with a poet’s grace. Trans scientists, hackers, and artists inscribe their bench confessions alongside hormone-poems, creating a laboratory for language that overwrites the cis-tem’s binaries. This first spring edition blooms with the data of desire and the longing for a science that holds our bodies whole.

fragments.text: A lab notebook for the trans-corporeal, where the monsoon of identity rewrites the protocols, turning gels into gossamer.

Pin_BioTranslab_rearranged.pdf.title: BioTranslab: Rearranged Documentation
Pin_BioTranslab_rearranged.pdf.analysis: A reassembled archive of the BioTranslab, Paula Pin’s nomadic wetlab for gynecological self-experimentation. Pap smears performed under kitchen microscopes, DIY speculums made from repurposed spoons, and microbial transfeminist rituals are collaged with poetic instructions and blurred photographs. Rearranged like dismembered tissue re-cultivated in a petri dish, the zine refuses linear narrative in favor of a cartography of cellular rebellion.

fragments.text: A cartography drawn with vaginal mucus and solder flux; the BioTranslab spills out of the zine and into the body’s damp territories.

fanzineAlcuirmiaLastversionLogos_new.pdf.title: Alcuirmia: Queer/Trans Bio‑Hacks Fanzine
fanzineAlcuirmiaLastversionLogos_new.pdf.analysis: A grimoire of alchemical protocols for queer and trans bodies: recipes for hormone-balancing tinctures, herbal contraceptives brewed from Mugwort and Cotton Root Bark, DIY mycology for mental ecology, and incantations against regulatory capture. The ‘Alcuirmia’ name fuses alcurnia (lineage) with alquimia (alchemy), reclaiming ancestral herbal knowledge as a form of biotechnological resistance. This last version carries the collective’s new logos—sigils of autonomy.

fragments.text: An anti-colonial brew simmering in the shadow of the clinic; each recipe is an act of vegetative rebellion, a spore print of transfeminist survival.

DIY-microscopy_HomemadeBook_full.pdf.title: DIY Microscopy: The Homemade Book (Full Edition)
DIY-microscopy_HomemadeBook_full.pdf.analysis: A comprehensive, pixel-dense tome that guides the maker through the entire microcosmos on a hacker budget. Starting from a hacked USB webcam and a laser pointer, the book traverses brightfield, darkfield, and fluorescence microscopy, staining with kitchen spices, and 3D-printing modular stages. Each chapter is a rite of passage that transforms old laptop parts into windows onto the invisible.

fragments.text: A thick mycelial mat of knowledge; turn any corner of a tropical kitchen into a research institute by following its instructions.

DIY-microscopy_HomemadeBook_short.pdf.title: DIY Microscopy: The Homemade Book (Short Edition)
DIY-microscopy_HomemadeBook_short.pdf.analysis: A pocketable abridgement of the full microscopy opus, distilled into a weekend-doable protocol. The short edition keeps only the essential rites: hacking one webcam, building a simple stage, and preparing an onion skin specimen. It is a crash course in seeing the invisible, designed to be carried into the field and stained with coffee and chlorophyll.

fragments.text: A traveler’s spore print of the larger book; small enough to slip into a backpack but potent enough to change how you see the jungle.

Synbio_for_Artists_Handbook_IGEM09-book..title: Synbio for Artists: iGEM09 Handbook
Synbio_for_Artists_Handbook_IGEM09-book..analysis: A time-capsule from the early days of DIY synthetic biology, translated for artistic minds. The handbook introduces BioBricks, genetic circuits, and the ethos of abstraction that would later grow into the biohacker movement. With ethical provocations and lab safety poetry, it invited artists to treat the cell as a canvas – years before CRISPR entered the chat.

fragments.text: A fossil of a future that is still arriving – its ideas have seeded countless tropical bio-labs, evolving far beyond the handbook’s original script.

Cheese_CRISPR_booklet_jap.pdf.title: CRISPR Cheese: A Booklet of Edible Genomics (Japanese Edition)
Cheese_CRISPR_booklet_jap.pdf.analysis: A culinary zine that curdles gene editing into a recipe book: CRISPR protocols are re-written as fermentation rituals for post-natural cheese. Through the lens of casein mutations and bacterial cultures, the booklet speculates on the terroir of the genome and the taste of edited inheritance. The Japanese edition adds local dairy folklore and calls for a microbial sovereignty against industrial cheese’s monocultures.

fragments.text: A kitchen-scale prophecy where the cow and the microbe meet the editing scaffold; soy sauce and methylotrophic yeast ferment in the margins of the genome.

fermentlab-pixelache_2017_strasbourg-zin.title: FermentLab Pixelache (Part 1): Inoculating the Network
fermentlab-pixelache_2017_strasbourg-zin.analysis: First portal in a five-part dispatch tracing the transborder microbial commons between Strasbourg and Helsinki. Pixelache's FermentLab maps the movement of symbiotic cultures—SCOBYs sealed in diplomatic jars, wild yeast starters passed through airport security as 'art supplies'—as living data packets. A hacker-ethnography of fermentation that treats each kitchen as a node, each floating pellicle an encrypted message from the vegetal internet.

fragments.text: SCOBYs travel better than people. A Helsinki mother-culture, birthed in a 1920s pharmacy, now ferments in Strasbourg's municipal heat. Taste is a timestamp.

fermentlab-pixelache_2017_strasbourg-zin.title: FermentLab Pixelache (Part 2): Makgeolli Mesh Protocols
fermentlab-pixelache_2017_strasbourg-zin.analysis: The second issue dives into nuruk fermentation and rice wine networks as a model for mesh networking. Finnish microbrewers and Alsatian bakers exchange grain amylases like routing tables. Documents a 'Makgeolli Mess Dinner' where participants drank from a common bowl linked to a CO2 sensor; when fermentation peaked, a MIDI chime played across six timezones. Recipes are given as modular function calls.

fragments.text: A batch of makgeolli froze in Helsinki Airport cargo hold. Thawed, it tasted of pineapple and data loss. We drank it anyway.

fermentlab-pixelache_2017_strasbourg-zin.title: FermentLab Pixelache (Part 3): Lactobacillus juris
fermentlab-pixelache_2017_strasbourg-zin.analysis: An ethnography of a legal hack: patenting an open-source lactobacillus strain called Lactobacillus juris, derived from the saliva of a public fermentation ritual. The zine archives the workshop where 50 people chewed organic maize, spat into a sterilized vat, and signed a copyleft transfer agreement. Includes a flowchart for 'Distributed Oral Consent' and a contract written in pH strips.

fragments.text: The strain still lives. It's a flavour attorney, sharp and sour, representing the microbiome in all future trade agreements.

fermentlab-pixelache_2018_strasbourg-zin.title: FermentLab Pixelache (Part 4): SCOBY Underland
fermentlab-pixelache_2018_strasbourg-zin.analysis: A journey into the dark, humid underspaces of both cities: abandoned railway tunnels in Helsinki turned tempeh incubators, the thermal vents of Strasbourg's ancient district heating used to accelerate miso maturation. The zine is a speculative infrastructure proposal where the city's waste heat network becomes a distributed fermentorium. Each page is a cross-section: concrete, mycelium, steam pipe, pickling jar.

fragments.text: Found a 3-year-old forgotten batch of miso in a steam tunnel. The caretaker said it was 'municipal umami'. We believe him.

fermentlab-pixelache_2018_strasbourg-zin.title: FermentLab Pixelache (Part 5): Endospore Broadcast
fermentlab-pixelache_2018_strasbourg-zin.analysis: Final transmission. The zine takes the form of a last will and testament for a dying SCOBY line, inviting fifty households to receive a tiny hyaluronic fragment in a tamper-proof spore strip. Each recipient becomes a seed bank. The text is a meditation on cryopreservation failure, microbial mourning, and the radical act of lyophilizing community. Concludes with a 'FermentLab Dispersal Ceremony' liturgy.

fragments.text: The mother SCOBY did not die. It just underwent a phase change into a thousand smaller lives. Protocol complete.

FoodPhreaking_03.pdf.title: FoodPhreaking_03: Gut Gardening
FoodPhreaking_03.pdf.analysis: A radical issue dedicated to the body as the ultimate fermentation vessel. 'Gut Gardening' repositions the human microbiome as a plot of land to be seeded, weeded, and harvested. Contains protocols for autologous fecal transplant yoghurts, a 'Fermented Self' sensory diary template, and a reverse-probiotic recipe where kimchi inoculates you, not the other way around. The ethnography follows a group of Swedish 'gut gardeners' who treat their intestines as community gardens, mapping bacterial terroir with DIY sequencing rigs.

fragments.text: One participant made a 'fecal jam' from a donor who ate only mangoes for a week. The jam was bright orange and smelled like heaven and rot. They called it 'Mango Tango Trans-corporeal'.

Nata_de_Coco.pdf.title: Nata_de_Coco: Membrane Kino
Nata_de_Coco.pdf.analysis: A hands-on zine transforming the popular Filipino dessert into a citizen biomaterial platform. Step-by-step guide to culturing bacterial cellulose (nata de coco) from coconut water and Acetobacter xylinum, then processing it into paper, leather-like fabric, and edible structured film. Documents a workshop in a Quezon City hacker kitchen where membranes were embedded with LED flasher circuits to make 'living kino' — short animations played on a sheet of growing pellicle. Interspecies cinema.

fragments.text: The nata film projector trapped a mosquito inside its pellicle. The mosquito became a 24-hour feature: 'Mosquito in the Membrane'. We charged 5 pesos.

Food_Phreaking.pdf.title: Food_Phreaking (Issue 00): Singapore Food Utopia
Food_Phreaking.pdf.analysis: The zeroth issue of the series, a speculative ethnography of Singapore's hawker centres reimagined as fully automated, microbe-managed food nodes. Each hawker stall is a bioreactor; dishes are designed by generative adversarial networks trained on grandma recipes. The zine narrates a fiction where the '30 by 30' food security plan succeeds through community fermentation lockers installed in Housing Development Board void decks, turning the city-state into a giant kimchi pot. Real interviews with hawkers about their microbial heritage are woven in.

fragments.text: An old uncle told us his shrimp paste (hae bee hiam) was alive for 40 years inside a ceramic jar. He never cleans the jar. 'That's the starter culture of my family.' The jar is a database.

Fanzine_MiculMicul_ByArtMatters.pdf.title: Fanzine Micul Micul by ArtMatters
Fanzine_MiculMicul_ByArtMatters.pdf.analysis: A vibrant Polish fanzine produced as part of ArtMatters' outreach. Mixes lithography with petri dish photography, profiling sixteen contemporary bio-artists who work with slime molds, cheese rind microbes, and sourdough. Central fold-out is a 'Microbial Art Gallery' where drawings are made with bioluminescent bacteria on agar plates, then scanned. The tone is playful, a zine for children and adults that asks: 'If your sourdough starter could vote, would it elect a yeast coalition?'

fragments.text: A child painted a penis with E. coli modified to glow green. The teacher said it was the most beautiful piece of microbial art she'd seen. The penis glowed for 20 hours.

RAT CATHCER_ISI_HVS100_2MK LONG_@2X.pdf.title: RAT CATCHER (ISI_HVS100_2MK LONG_@2X.pdf)
RAT CATHCER_ISI_HVS100_2MK LONG_@2X.pdf.analysis: A raw, full-resolution documentation of the feral urban stratum as seen through the rat-catchers of Jakarta. Not a pest control manual; an ecological ethnography of the symbiotic loop between food waste, municipal fermentation, and Rattus norvegicus. The zine details how traditional rat-catchers read garbage piles like an oracle, tasting the 'brew' of a drain to predict rat movements. Includes a field recipe for 'Drain Tempeh'—a fermented food made from discarded soy pulp rescued from rat habitat, its safety monitored by the feral knowledge of the catcher. The filename refers to a high-voltage security scan of a 2-meter-long trap route; the PDF itself is heavily encrypted 'so the rats don't read it.'

fragments.text: A rat-catcher named Om Juki told us: 'The rat who eats fermented mango learns the taste of tomorrow's flood.' We didn't understand until the monsoon came.

RAT CATHCER_COVER_IV230_2MK LONG_2X.pdf.title: RAT CATCHER COVER (IV230_2MK LONG_2X.pdf)
RAT CATHCER_COVER_IV230_2MK LONG_2X.pdf.analysis: The standalone cover art for the Rat Catcher zine, a high-voltage slow-scan image of a 2-meter-long drainpipe cross-section transformed into a technicolour mandala. The image is a superposition of a scanning electron micrograph of Leptospira bacteria, a rat's pawprint, and a satellite map of Jakarta's garbage truck routes. Overlaid text reads 'IN RAT WE TRUST / BEBAS DARI RACUN (FREE FROM POISON)'. The 'IV230' code refers to the voltage used to ionize the pipe's gas content, revealing a ghostly glow interpreted as the rats' 'feral ether'. Printed at 2x scale as a ritual object, placed at rat holes to invite a reciprocal truce.

fragments.text: We placed the printed cover by a storm drain. The next morning, it had been gnawed in a pattern that matched the rabies-inoculation map. Message received.

WaftLab-OpenLab_2024.pdf.title: WaftLab-OpenLab_2024.pdf
WaftLab-OpenLab_2024.pdf.analysis: A community-sourced zine documenting WaftLab, a nomadic open laboratory that moves between wet markets, volcanic fumaroles, and fishing villages in Yogyakarta. The 2024 edition focuses on 'Volcanic fermentation': using hot sulfuric gases to accelerate tempeh fermentation and create pickled eggs with a blue sheen. Includes lab notebooks scanned in high-res, showing bacterial colony drawings made with local dyes from indigo and dragon fruit. The zine is a living document that updates via a shared Telegram bot where farmers report mold growth on experiments.

fragments.text: We fermented rice in a Merapi fumarole for 3 hours. It turned neon pink and the local geomancer said it 'spoke the mountain's verses'. We ate it with respect and got mild auditory hallucinations.

GOSH2026_Leaflet-shortside.pdf.title: GOSH2026_Leaflet-shortside.pdf
GOSH2026_Leaflet-shortside.pdf.analysis: A speculative leaflet retrieved from the year 2026, designed for the Gathering for Open Science Hardware held in a floating observatory over a Sumatra peat swamp. The zine advertises workshops like 'Fermenting Microcontrollers: Power your Arduino with a live tempeh fuel cell' and 'SCOBY-based Sensors for Forest Canopy Networks'. The leaflet is designed as a tropical survival tool: it unfolds into a water-filter paper coated with microbial cellulose. Community events include 'The Great Peat Sauerkraut Cook-off' and a midnight ritual to calibrate open-source pH meters with probiotic tears.

fragments.text: This leaflet was found inside a hollowed-out durian, delivered by drone. The smell was proof of origin. We trust the fruit more than the wireless signal.

Fanzine Mingapa Bigini Mingapa Bigitu.pd.title: Fanzine Mingapa Bigini Mingapa Bigitu.pdf
Fanzine Mingapa Bigini Mingapa Bigitu.pd.analysis: A grassroots Indonesian fanzine whose title loosely translates to 'Why is it like this, why is it like that?' A publication of the Kepurun Bio-Community in Central Java, exploring ancestral food fermentation and its intersection with digital culture. The issue details an event where villagers recreated a 9th-century inscription's recipe for 'ciamsiu' (fermented rice wine) using a 3D-reconstructed clay pot and a temperature controller made from a recycled rice cooker. The zine is full of hand-drawn illustrations, SMS-style narratives, and a comic strip where a tempeh mold spore guides you through the internet of beans.

fragments.text: Pak Darto, 73, tasted the 3D-printed jar ciamsiu and said: 'Same spirit, new body. The microbes remember even if we forget.' The photocopier broke from the humidity, but we kept the jammer as a relic.

A3_Poster_wormolution_LessText.pdf.title: A3_Poster_wormolution_LessText.pdf
A3_Poster_wormolution_LessText.pdf.analysis: A large-format A3 poster-zine, minimal-text manifesto for the Wormolution movement: a global uprising of vermicomposting hackers who see earthworms as planetary digestive healers. The poster maps worm-based bioremediation projects in five tropical cities, pairing each with a fermented food: Manila worm-castings-gin, Nairobi worm-compost injera, Jakarta earthworm tempeh enhancer. The centre graphic is a Lumbricus system blueprint, a wormery designed to break down e-waste plastics using co-fermented microbial-worm guts. The 'LessText' directive means all communication is done via worm trails; the PDF is a scan of a large compost bed where worms were seeded with colored cornmeal to write the poster's text on the surface over 7 days.

fragments.text: The worms wrote 'NO LESS THAN SOIL' in cornmeal across a 2-meter bed. A rat came and ate the 'SOIL', leaving 'NO LESS THAN'. We let it stand as the final manifesto.

KrautsourceEnergy.pdf.title: Krautsource Energy
KrautsourceEnergy.pdf.analysis: A pungent guide to harvesting electrons from lactic acid chaos. Sauerkraut, coconut toddy, and tapai fermentations become living bio-batteries that power small soil sensors, LED beacons, and ultra-low-power noise circuits. Includes mud-to-microbe circuit diagrams.

GBMN_redesigned_Print.pdf.title: Global Bio-Media Network Redesigned Print
GBMN_redesigned_Print.pdf.analysis: Redesigned manual for the Global Bio-Media Network: interlinking fungal sensor nodes, crystal radio transmitters built from old phone parts, and mycelial data streams across a ruined plantation. A hacker-ethnographer’s map of bio-digital communication outside the internet.

Instruction_Wurmophon_leaflet_shortside..title: Wurmophon Instruction Leaflet
Instruction_Wurmophon_leaflet_shortside..analysis: Instructions for the Wurmophon, an earthworm sound synthesizer. Piezo pickups buried in vermicompost translate peristaltic wriggles into sub-bass rumbles and microtonal chirps. A mud-op-amp circuit and a call to listen to the soil’s hidden rhythm section.

Fanzine_Powerharvest_english.pdf.title: Powerharvest (English)
Fanzine_Powerharvest_english.pdf.analysis: A fanzine on DIY energy harvesting for guerrilla electronics. Schematics for drawing trickle currents from soil microbial fuel cells, stray AM radio waves, tree-potential differences, and the sweat of a dancer. Off-grid power for a sonic network hidden in the humid dark.

biohaha-helmi_hardian-angela_sunaryo-zin.title: Sensewalking Flux (Indonesian Edition)
biohaha-helmi_hardian-angela_sunaryo-zin.analysis: A psychogeographic protocol tuned to the tropics. Hand-built humidity sensors, geophones, and ethnobotanical notebooks map the invisible flows beneath Jakarta’s pavement. Footstep rhythms, soil moisture, and insect stridulation recorded as a flux cartography. Bahasa Indonesia text.

DIRT_artscienceBLR_Handbook-2011.pdf.title: DIRT – Art-Science Handbook (Bengaluru 2011)
DIRT_artscienceBLR_Handbook-2011.pdf.analysis: A compendium from the DIRT collective in Bengaluru: soil chromatography, microbial glues for brick making, electro-culture experiments, and ferment as political resistance. A celebration of dirt as both material and metaphor, stitched together with photocopier grit and masala stains.

Fungal_Bioreactor_Guide_DE.pdf.title: Fungal Bioreactor Guide (Deutsch)
Fungal_Bioreactor_Guide_DE.pdf.analysis: Bauanleitung für einen Low-Tech-Mykoreaktor aus alten Dampfkochtöpfen. Pilzmyzelien bauen Toxine ab und fruchten zu Austernpilzen. Mit Plänen für Feuchtigkeitssensorik und Sporenabdrücken unter dem Tropenhimmel. Deutsch.

Fungal_Bioreactor_Guide_EN.pdf.title: Fungal Bioreactor Guide (English)
Fungal_Bioreactor_Guide_EN.pdf.analysis: Step-by-step guide to building a fungal bioreactor from repurposed kitchen ware. Cultivate oyster mushrooms while mycelial webs digest oil, pesticides, and heavy metals. Humidity hacks, spore printing, and recipes for post-remediation harvests in a monsoon climate.

A3_Homemade2025_poster.pdf.title: Homemade 2025 Gathering Poster
A3_Homemade2025_poster.pdf.analysis: A3 risograph poster summoning bio-hackers, fermenters, and soil alchemists to a hidden tropical convergence. Cyber-botanical vines twist around circuit traces and mycelial maps, while earth battery symbols glow like monsoon fireflies. A promise of wetware, wild yeasts, and low-power sound under the canopy.

Cover_Print Layout.pdf.title: Noise MiniZine – Cover
Cover_Print Layout.pdf.analysis: A screen-printed chaos net of circuit-bent scribbles, rotting tropical fruit, and glitched-out photocopy textures. The cover crackles with lo-fi promise, its title hand-etched with a salvaged soldering iron. This is the manifesto of static, fuzz, and monsoon feedback.

Inside_Mini-Zine Print Layout.pdf.title: Noise MiniZine – Inside
Inside_Mini-Zine Print Layout.pdf.analysis: Schematic spells for no-input mixers, singing solar cells, and tin-can microphones. Annotations mix English with Bahasa Pasar and solder burns. Step-by-step rituals for coaxing noise from discarded jungle junk, celebrating the beauty of broken signals.

cap1_fanzina.pdf.title: Fanzina Chapter 1 – Electric Mangrove
cap1_fanzina.pdf.analysis: First chapter of the electronics and sound-art fanzine. Floating mangrove roots become distributed antennas; brackish water batteries power tiny oscillators. A field guide to listening to the electric potential between mud, leaf, and salt.

cap2_fanzina.pdf.title: Fanzina Chapter 2 – Rust Potentiometers
cap2_fanzina.pdf.analysis: Second chapter: transforming oxidation into resistance, crafting variable resistors from sun-baked mud, corrosion, and wire scraps. Diagrams for building touch-sensitive sound generators that smell of monsoon rust.

cap3_fanzina.pdf.title: Fanzina Chapter 3 – Feedback Rituals
cap3_fanzina.pdf.analysis: Closing chapter: using acoustic feedback loops in abandoned structures as instruments. Leyden jar capacitors, bamboo flutes as waveform guides, and the wild howl of the tropics turned into a participatory sonic ceremony.

Zine_ES_cromatografia-circular-de-suelos.title: Circular Soil Chromatography Guide (Español)
Zine_ES_cromatografia-circular-de-suelos.analysis: Guía de cromatografía circular de suelos: filtros de café impregnados con nitrato de plata revelan mandalas de humus, halos microbianos y zonas minerales. Una práctica alquímica de bajo costo desde los márgenes tropicales. Español.

Zine_IND_panduan-kromatografi-mandala-ta.title: Circular Soil Chromatography Guide (Bahasa Indonesia)
Zine_IND_panduan-kromatografi-mandala-ta.analysis: Panduan kromatografi tanah melingkar: dengan penyaring kopi dan perak nitrat, tanah-tanah tropis menggambar riwayatnya sendiri dalam cincin-cincin warna. Teknik rakyat untuk membaca kesuburan dan racun. Bahasa Indonesia.

Zine_EN_soil-chromatography-guide_2022_d.title: Circular Soil Chromatography Guide (English)
Zine_EN_soil-chromatography-guide_2022_d.analysis: Circular soil chromatography: a low-tech art-science practice. Coffee filters wick silver nitrate through earth samples, painting mandalas of fertility, microbial activity, and contamination. The zine transforms the kitchen table into a soil alchemist’s laboratory.

Chroma-zine_Workshop-edition_EN_2025-dig.title: Soil Chromatography Workshop Edition – Basic Field Protocol
Chroma-zine_Workshop-edition_EN_2025-dig.analysis: Hands-on workshop booklet: preparing silver nitrate solution, mixing soil slurries, and developing chromatograms in the shade of a banana tree. Templates for collective reading and first interpretations of the rings. Bound for humid field use.

Chromatography_Workshop_edition_ESP.pdf.title: Soil Chromatography Workshop Edition – Advanced Interpretation
Chromatography_Workshop_edition_ESP.pdf.analysis: Advanced interpretation guide: reading the humus ring, enzymatic zones, and mineral spikes. Charts linking color bands to microbial respiration and heavy-metal presence. A hacker’s syntax for the soil’s own visual language, co-created in workshops across Java.

Soil_Micro_Zine_Ind_2023_1_print.pdf.title: Soil Microscopy Zine (Bahasa Indonesia)
Soil_Micro_Zine_Ind_2023_1_print.pdf.analysis: Panduan komprehensif pengamatan tanah dengan mikroskop rakitan dari kamera web bekas. Nematoda, rotifera, dan benang mikoriza menari di bawah lensa. Lensa tetesan air dan pencahayaan LED dari hutan. Bahasa Indonesia.

Soil_Micro_Zine_Esp_2022-05_digital.pdf.title: Soil Microscopy Zine (Español)
Soil_Micro_Zine_Esp_2022-05_digital.pdf.analysis: Guía exhaustiva de microscopía de suelos con lentes reciclados. Descubra el universo de tardígrados, colémbolos y redes fúngicas. Instrucciones para construir una platina, iluminación con LED y captura de imágenes en la selva. Español.

Soil_Micro_Zine_De_2023-01_digital.pdf.title: Soil Microscopy Zine (Deutsch)
Soil_Micro_Zine_De_2023-01_digital.pdf.analysis: Bodenmikroskopie für Alle: Bau eines Mikroskops aus einer alten Webcam. Nematoden, Bärtierchen und Pilzhyphen in atemberaubender Nähe. Beleuchtung mit Fahrradlampen und feuchten Petrischalen im Tropenlabor. Deutsch.

Soil_Micro_Zine_En_print_1x_148x210.pdf.title: Soil Microscopy Zine (English)
Soil_Micro_Zine_En_print_1x_148x210.pdf.analysis: A comprehensive guide to soil life under a hacked lens. Transform a discarded webcam into a field microscope and plunge into the dramas of nematodes, rotifers, mycorrhizal hyphae, and microarthropods. Step-by-step builds, LED lighting tricks, and image capture techniques for the humid jungle lab.

3x-A3_Soillife_Illustration.png.title: SOIL LIFE ILLUSTRATION (3x A3 POSTER)
3x-A3_Soillife_Illustration.png.analysis: A massive triple-A3 visual cartography of the subterranean undercommons. This illustration maps the complex trophic webs of the rhizosphere, where fungal hyphae weave through mineral grains and nematodes navigate the moist voids of the humus. It acts as a macroscopic window into the microscopic drama of soil regeneration, visualizing the chemical signals and symbiotic exchanges that sustain all terrestrial life.

fragments.text: The rhizosphere is not a boundary but a bridge—a molecular marketplace where sugar is traded for phosphorus and water.
To see the soil is to understand the metabolism of the planet.
